hints: Work done against friction is friction magnitude multiplied by the $120\,\mathrm m$ distance from A to B.
Resolve vertically: the upward component $25\sin36^\circ$ reduces the normal reaction, so $R+25\sin36^\circ=4g$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: Resolve forces perpendicular to the horizontal road to find normal reaction $R$:
The pulling force of $25\text{ N}$ acts at $36^\circ$ above the horizontal, having an upward vertical component $25\sin 36^\circ$:
$$R + 25\sin 36^\circ = mg = 4(10) = 40\text{ N}$$
$$R = 40 - 25\sin 36^\circ = 40 - 25(0.587785) = 40 - 14.6946 = 25.3054\text{ N}$$

Step 2: Calculate the frictional force $F$ using $F = \mu R$ with $\mu = 0.4$:
$$F = 0.4 \times 25.3054 = 10.1222\text{ N}$$

Step 3: Calculate the work done against friction over the distance $d = 120\text{ m}$:
$$W_{\text{friction}} = F \times d = 10.1222 \times 120 = 1214.66\text{ J} \approx 1210\text{ J}$$
The work done against friction is $1210\text{ J}$ (or $1215\text{ J}$).

hints: Apply the work-energy principle from A to B, using the work against friction found in part (a).
The pulling force does forward work $(25\cos36^\circ)(120)$; its vertical component does no work because the displacement is horizontal.
Solve for $v_B^2$ and take the positive square root for the speed at B.
walkthrough:
Step 1: Calculate the work done by the constant pulling force over the displacement $d = 120\text{ m}$:
Only the horizontal component of the pulling force ($25\cos 36^\circ$) does work:
$$W_{\text{pull}} = (25\cos 36^\circ) \times 120 = 25(0.809017) \times 120 = 2427.05\text{ J}$$

Step 2: Express the change in kinetic energy of the $4\text{ kg}$ block from initial speed $u = 7\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to final speed $v_B$:
$$\Delta E_k = \frac{1}{2}m v_B^2 - \frac{1}{2}m u^2 = \frac{1}{2}(4)v_B^2 - \frac{1}{2}(4)(7^2) = 2v_B^2 - 98$$

Step 3: Apply the work-energy principle:
$$\Delta E_k = W_{\text{pull}} - W_{\text{friction}}$$
$$2v_B^2 - 98 = 2427.05 - 1214.66 = 1212.39$$
$$2v_B^2 = 1212.39 + 98 = 1310.39$$
$$v_B^2 = \frac{1310.39}{2} = 655.195$$
$$v_B = \sqrt{655.195} \approx 25.5968\text{ m s}^{-1} \approx 25.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
The speed of the block at $B$ is $25.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
